text.p: Omniquip International Inc said Tuesday its backlog rose to $116 million at the end of the fiscal second quarter from $77 million as of December 31.
Additional orders from the military accounted for $14 million of the $39 million increase in backlog for the second quarter, which ended March 31.
Earlier, Omniquip reported second quarter earnings of $0.35 a share, up from $0.12 a year ago.

"Our excellent second quarter performance was due to a number of factors including the increased sales and earnings generated by the acquisition of Lull International in August 1996, continued growth in the market for telescopic material handlers and improved manufacturing efficiencies at all three of our plants," P. Enoch Stiff, president, said in a statement.
